selected_items.author: github
selected_items.text: Kimi K2.7 Code is the first open-weight model you can select in the GitHub Copilot model picker. What does that mean for you? @burkeholland explains how this low-cost, high-performance model gives you more choice and flexibility in your workflow.
selected_items.selection_reason: Concrete product news: first open-weight model (Kimi K2.7 Code) selectable in the GitHub Copilot picker, distinct from prior Sonnet 5 GA item.

selected_items.author: minchoi
selected_items.text: This is actually useful. LangChain just released OpenWiki. It's an open-source agent that creates a wiki for your codebase, connects it to your coding agent, and keeps it updated as your repo changes. Your AI coding agent gets long-term repo context without stuffing everything into context.
selected_items.selection_reason: Concrete open-source release: LangChain OpenWiki, an agent that builds and maintains a codebase wiki for coding agents.

selected_items.author: akshay_pachaar
selected_items.text: Don't train the model, evolve the harness. I read a brilliant blog post from Hugging Face where they took a frozen open model scoring 0% on a hard legal agent benchmark, left its weights alone, and let an automated loop rewrite only the code around it. That code layer is the real system.
selected_items.selection_reason: Strong technical analysis of a Hugging Face experiment where only the agent harness code was evolved around a frozen model to lift benchmark performance.

selected_items.author: edzitron
selected_items.text: One of the biggest lies of the AI bubble is that Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta are growing because of AI. In reality, they're using the continued growth of their other business units to cover the meager returns from AI, and the massive waste of their trillion-plus in capex.
selected_items.selection_reason: High-engagement critical analysis arguing big-tech revenue growth masks weak direct AI returns against heavy capex.

selected_items.author: karlmehta
selected_items.text: Yann LeCun, Meta's chief AI scientist and a Turing Award winner, explains why scaling up LLMs will never reach human-level AI, and names the four things today's systems still can't do.
selected_items.selection_reason: Practitioner-shared argument from Yann LeCun on the limits of LLM scaling toward human-level AI; distinct named-source technical viewpoint.

selected_items.author: testingcatalog
selected_items.text: Condense.chat has opened access to its new compression proxy, which sits between a coding AI agent and the model, cutting the token bill. Two in-house models handle the work: Helene 1 strips unnecessary tokens before they hit cache. Adeline 1 compacts settled agent loops.
selected_items.selection_reason: Concrete product launch: Condense.chat compression proxy with two in-house models (Helene 1, Adeline 1) to reduce coding-agent token costs.

selected_items.author: bigaiguy
selected_items.text: A Samsung researcher just quietly humiliated every trillion-dollar AI lab on Earth. Her name is Alexia Jolicoeur-Martineau, a Senior AI Researcher at Samsung's SAIT lab in Montreal. In October she published a paper called Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks.
selected_items.selection_reason: Names a concrete paper and researcher (Samsung SAIT, Tiny Recursion, Less is More) as a distinct technical story on small recursive-reasoning networks.

selected_items.author: vicky_grok
selected_items.text: Anthropic pays $750,000+ a year for engineers who can build LLM architectures from scratch. Stanford taught the entire thing in a 1 hour lecture and released it for free.
selected_items.selection_reason: Practitioner resource contrasting Anthropic's LLM-architect pay band with a free Stanford lecture on building LLMs from scratch.

selected_items.author: Hesamation
selected_items.text: when a researcher from OpenAI, DeepMind, and Stanford drops an article like this, you know it's a must-read. TL;DR: execution is cheaper with AI. the edge is choosing the right problems, building strong connections, and investing real time.
selected_items.selection_reason: Widely shared practitioner analysis arguing that with AI execution cheap, competitive edge shifts to problem selection, relationships and time investment.

selected_items.author: dr_cintas
selected_items.text: ONE GITHUB REPO has every permanently free AI API with real rate limits - no trials that expire, no cards needed, just models that stay free forever. Not signup-credit stuff that runs out in a week, these are the tiers that stay free.
selected_items.selection_reason: Practitioner resource: a GitHub repo cataloguing permanently free AI/LLM APIs with real rate limits.
